slots.practicalActivity: In Setup, open Object Manager for an object you know well (such as Opportunity) and list every declarative automation tool available on it (validation rules, approval processes, flow, assignment/escalation rules), writing one real business rule each could enforce.
slots.deliverable: A written list mapping each declarative tool available on one object to a real business rule it could enforce.

slots.practicalActivity: In a sandbox or Developer Edition org, start a new approval process on Opportunity with the Standard Setup Wizard: set Entry Criteria to Amount > 50000, leave editability at Administrators Only, and pick or create a simple email template for notifications. Do not activate it yet.
slots.deliverable: One approval process on Opportunity configured through entry criteria, editability, and a notification template, saved but not yet activated.

slots.practicalActivity: Add 2 approval steps to the Opportunity approval process from the previous lesson: Step 1 routes to the Opportunity Owner's manager for discounts up to 25%, Step 2 routes to a named Sales Director for anything higher, then activate the process and submit a test record through each tier.
slots.deliverable: One activated 2-step approval process on Opportunity, with a test record successfully routed through each tier.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a validation rule on Opportunity requiring Close Date to be in the future for any newly created record, then test it against one record that should be blocked and one that should save cleanly.
slots.deliverable: One validation rule on Opportunity, tested against one failing and one passing record with the actual error message shown.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a formula field on Opportunity named Discount_Tier__c that uses nested IF functions to return "Standard", "Manager Review", or "Director Review" based on the discount percentage, and test it on 3 records spanning all 3 tiers.
slots.deliverable: One formula field returning the correct tier label on each of 3 test records spanning all 3 outcomes.

slots.practicalActivity: Create an Email Alert tied to your Opportunity approval process so the assigned approver is notified when a request reaches their step, then submit a test record and confirm the alert fired using Setup's email log or your own inbox.
slots.deliverable: One Email Alert attached to the approval process, with confirmed evidence it fired on a real test submission.

slots.practicalActivity: On a second object you have not yet touched (such as Case or Quote), independently build a complete declarative stack from scratch: one validation rule, one formula field, and a one-step approval process with its own Email Alert, choosing the business scenario yourself.
slots.deliverable: A second object's full declarative stack: a validation rule, a formula field, and an approval process with an Email Alert, independently built.

slots.practicalActivity: For 3 realistic requirements (a simple field-update rule, a multi-object callout to an external system, and a complex multi-currency calculation), write which tool you would choose — validation rule, Flow, or Apex — and justify each choice in one sentence.
slots.deliverable: A written decision table covering 3 scenarios, each with a chosen tool and a one-sentence justification.

slots.practicalActivity: Draw or outline the order-of-execution sequence for a single record save on an object with both a validation rule and an approval process (where validation rules fire relative to before-save automation, and where approval-process entry checks fall), checking it against your own Opportunity setup from Chapter 1.
slots.deliverable: A written or diagrammed order-of-execution sequence, checked against the real automation on your own Opportunity object.

slots.practicalActivity: Inspect your Discount_Tier__c-dependent automation from Chapter 1 for a scenario where an update could re-trigger itself (for example a flow that updates the same field it checks), and add an explicit guard condition that prevents the record from re-entering the same automation unnecessarily.
slots.deliverable: One automation with a documented, tested recursion guard preventing it from unnecessarily re-triggering itself.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an automation inventory covering everything created in Chapter 1 (validation rules, formula fields, approval processes, Email Alerts): object, purpose, owner, and last-modified date for each.
slots.deliverable: A written automation inventory table covering every automation built so far in this course.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick one tool choice you made in Chapter 1 (for example building a validation rule instead of a flow) and write a one-page case for why the opposite choice would also have worked, including what trade-off your original choice accepted.
slots.deliverable: A written one-page trade-off analysis revisiting one earlier tool choice from the opposite direction.

lessons.title: Business Process Case Study: Quote Approval

slots.practicalActivity: Build Harborline Industrial Supply's Quote Discount Approval exactly as designed: entry criteria Quote.Status = Submitted AND Discount_Percent__c > 10, Step 1 to the Quote Owner's manager for 10-25%, Step 2 to a named Sales Director above 25%, record locking on while pending, and distinct final-approval/final-rejection actions.
slots.deliverable: One activated two-step Quote Discount Approval process matching the case study's design, tested with a 15% and a 30% discount quote.

lessons.title: Business Process Case Study: Service Level Escalation

slots.practicalActivity: Build the lesson's Service Level Escalation design on Case: entry criteria based on time-since-created or SLA breach, an automated reassignment or Priority escalation action, and a logged record of the escalation, tested against a Case that should escalate and one that should not.
slots.deliverable: One working SLA escalation automation on Case, tested against both an escalating and a non-escalating test record.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a handoff document for the Quote Discount Approval and Service Level Escalation automations you just built, covering entry criteria, approvers/actions, and how to test each one, as if handing the org to another admin tomorrow.
slots.deliverable: A written handoff document covering both case-study automations in enough detail for another admin to maintain them.

slots.practicalActivity: Complete the lesson's practice lab build exactly as instructed in your own org, assembling the validation rule, approval process, and notification pieces it specifies into one working end-to-end automation.
slots.deliverable: The practice lab's complete automation, built and activated in your own org exactly as instructed.

slots.practicalActivity: Write and run a 4-case test log against the practice-lab automation: 2 records that should pass/approve cleanly and 2 that should be blocked or escalated, recording the actual outcome of each.
slots.deliverable: A written test log with 4 test cases run against the practice-lab automation and their actual outcomes recorded.

slots.practicalActivity: Review every automation built across this chapter (both case studies and the practice lab) and confirm each one's entry criteria, locking behavior, and recursion safety still hold now that they coexist on the same org.
slots.deliverable: A written review confirming entry criteria, locking, and recursion safety hold across all of Chapter 3's automations together.

slots.practicalActivity: Invent a new fictional company and business complaint different from Harborline or the SLA case study, and design and build its approval or escalation automation end to end without lesson-by-lesson guidance.
slots.deliverable: An independently designed and built automation for an original fictional company and complaint.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page portfolio summary covering the Quote Discount Approval, the Service Level Escalation, the practice lab automation, and your own original automation, explaining the key design decision behind each.
slots.deliverable: A written portfolio summary of all 4 automations built in this chapter, each with its key design decision explained.

slots.practicalActivity: Invent a brand-new, never-before-seen stakeholder complaint (one sentence, deliberately vague), then write and answer the lesson's 5 discovery questions against it to turn that vague complaint into specific entry-criteria-ready requirements.
slots.deliverable: A written discovery Q&A that turns one invented vague complaint into specific, buildable requirements.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the requirements you just gathered, draw or outline a before-you-build process map showing each step, decision point, and role involved, before touching Setup.
slots.deliverable: A written or diagrammed process map for your invented stakeholder complaint, covering steps, decision points, and roles.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the actual automation your process map calls for in your own org (validation rule, approval process, and/or flow as needed) end to end with no further guidance, then write a final course portfolio summary covering every automation built across all 4 chapters of this course.
slots.deliverable: One newly built automation matching your own process map, plus a final written portfolio summary of every automation built across the whole course.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can design a complete declarative business process for a real stakeholder request: choosing between validation rules, approval processes and flows, building multi-step approval chains with correct entry criteria, locking and recursion safety, documenting and testing the result, and translating a vague stakeholder complaint into working, deployed automation.
